chains.name: Close the Staff SWE offer
chains.desc: Turns the $284K band-exception decision into an approved offer, filed memo and signed letter without leaving chat

steps.result: Offer packet pulled: $284,000 TC, req ENG-1187 open 74 days, competing offer expires Monday
Within band: 6.0% above $268K mid, under $290K max — validation ref CMP-2214
Exception memo HR-EXC-0093 filed with CFO note and one-off precedent guard
Offer letter sent for signature — envelope ENV-58217, expires Monday 18:00 CT

steps.args: to=Daniel Okafor, Tomas Rivera, James Whitfield
steps.result: Approval summary posted with memo and envelope links ahead of the 15:00 sync

chains.outcome: Offer approved in Greenhouse, band check CMP-2214 logged in Workday, memo HR-EXC-0093 filed to SharePoint, envelope ENV-58217 out via DocuSign, and all three approvers briefed in Teams before 15:00.

insight.headline: Req ENG-1187 sat open 74 days — nearly double the 38-day company average
insight.detail: Joining Greenhouse req age with Workday exit reasons shows the real cost of haggling: compensation already drives 34% of FY26 exits, so losing a closed candidate over a 6% band gap would feed the exact attrition driver the Sep 1 comp review targets. Greenhouse alone sees a slow req and Workday alone sees exit codes — only the join prices the delay.
insight.action: Pre-authorize band exceptions up to band max for any P1 req open past 60 days

insight.headline: Hires whose ServiceNow kit arrived late scored 0.9 points lower on the week-1 pulse
insight.detail: Correlating ServiceNow hardware delivery dates with Workday week-1 pulse scores against Greenhouse start dates shows late laptops dragging first-week sentiment from 4.4 toward 3.5. ServiceNow only tracks tickets and Workday only stores scores — neither system can see that day-1 readiness, not the program content, moves the pulse.
insight.action: Auto-raise the laptop request the moment any Greenhouse offer flips to accepted
